targetBasis: User pacing preference. No reviewed source establishes an exact universal two-second optimum or guarantees addictive viewing.

sources.title: YouTube: Shorts search and discovery
sources.finding: Choosing to view, average view duration/percentage viewed, likes and post-watch surveys inform Shorts ranking alongside personalization and outside factors.
sources.application: Prioritize a relevant hook, a complete story and viewer satisfaction. Do not invent ranking weights.

sources.title: YouTube: Shorts content analytics
sources.finding: Compare Shorts with Shorts and inspect both successful and weaker uploads. Viewer choice versus swiping is a distinct metric.
sources.application: Evaluate opening effectiveness separately from subsequent viewing; compare comparable uploads.

sources.title: YouTube: engagement metrics
sources.finding: Engaged viewing and duration measure different behavior from starts/replays. Shorts viewing duration uses engaged views and associated watch time.
sources.application: Timeline pacing cannot be labeled a measured retention score.

sources.title: YouTube: key moments for retention
sources.finding: Retention spikes may reflect enjoyable rewatching or confusing content; dips indicate abandoning or skipping portions.
sources.application: Keep source evidence legible and diagnose actual curves before assuming all replays are positive.

sources.title: YouTube Shorts deep dive: Todd Sherman and Jenny Hoyos
sources.finding: An experienced creator emphasizes the first-second hook and concise miniature stories.
sources.application: Aim for a relevant foreground visual by one second, followed by an actual payoff. This is practitioner guidance, not a controlled universal threshold.

sources.title: YouTube: how recommendations work
sources.finding: Recommendations use multiple personalized signals, including satisfaction surveys, rather than watch time alone.
sources.application: Maintain relevance, accuracy and a satisfying conclusion.

sources.title: TikTok Creative Codes
sources.finding: Hook/body/close structure, movement, transitions and purposeful music/voice/effects are recommended for ads.
sources.application: Adapt audiovisual storytelling techniques. Advertising recall and conversion results are not proof of organic gaming Shorts retention.

sources.title: TikTok AUNZ 2026 Creative Starter Pack
sources.finding: Connect the opening to the overall message; demonstrate the body clearly. One worked example uses clips of one to two seconds.
sources.application: Use brief meaningful developments as a design pattern, while preserving useful explanations and complete actions.

sources.title: TikTok and System1: creative fatigue and entertainment
sources.finding: The reported study involved 8,000 heavy TikTok users and explores repeated exposure, entertainment and creative variety.
sources.application: Vary staging and contextual humor across fresh versions. The ad exposure results do not guarantee performance for an individual gaming video.

sources.title: Wals et al.: The dynamic effects of visual complexity and scene cuts on viewer attention
sources.finding: Eye-tracking analysis of 2,520 viewing experiences across 42 public-service announcements associates shorter, visually simpler scenes with stronger attentional synchrony; complexity has a delayed negative association.
sources.application: Use frequent purposeful developments with one clear dominant focus and coordinated support. Attention synchrony in ads is not an exact watch-through probability or an optimum cut interval.

sources.title: Valuch et al.: The Effect of Cinematic Cuts on Human Attention
sources.finding: Repeated visual content across a cut supports faster attention relocation in a controlled sports-video task.
sources.application: Keep the established lead and spatial continuity while secondary elements change. The experiment is not a Shorts-feed retention test.

sources.title: Kumar et al.: Watch to Edit: Video Retargeting using Gaze
sources.finding: The method preserves salient regions and cinematographic constraints when adapting video framing; the reported user study favors it over comparison approaches.
sources.application: Retain important characters, faces and evidence in mobile framing instead of maximizing movement indiscriminately.

sources.title: Shifting Focus with HCEye
sources.finding: The study examines 27 participants viewing 150 webpages; dynamic highlighting remains salient under cognitive load, while attending to other elements becomes harder.
sources.application: Direct one primary visual focus at a time. This is a cautious design inference from webpages, not measured gaming-video retention.
